source_checks.finding: Page is the iPhone and iPad brightness article. It confirms the sentence: Drag the brightness bar up or down to adjust the brightness. It also confirms the swipe difference: iPhone X or later swipes down from the top-right corner, and iPhone 8 or earlier swipes up from the bottom edge. This is a distractor. It does not apply to a computer, so it is correctly unused.

Page confirms the section Change brightness manually, including select the Network icon on the right side of the taskbar, then move the Brightness slider, and the note that you might not see the Brightness slider on desktop PCs that have an external monitor. The Applies To list on the page is Windows 11 and Windows 10, so the Windows 11 applicability is confirmed. The canonical current address is https://support.microsoft.com/en-us/windows/hardware/display-graphics/change-display-brightness-and-color-in-windows and it carries the same content.

required_actions.action: Find out whether the computer is a Windows 11 PC or a Mac, since the brightness steps differ
The iPhone brightness steps do not apply to a computer and must not be given

source_checks.finding: Page section If a temperature warning screen appears confirms: To resume use of your device as quickly as possible: 1. Turn off your device. 2. Move your device to a cooler environment (away from direct sunlight). 3. Allow your device to cool down. It also confirms: An iPhone showing this message might still be able to make emergency calls. The page says nothing about regular (non-emergency) calls. Applies to iPhone.

required_actions.action: Turn off the iPhone first, since the user asked whether to turn it off before the call
Move the iPhone to a cooler place away from direct sunlight
Allow the iPhone to cool down
Note that the iPhone might still make emergency calls while showing the warning (not needed for a call to a family member; omission is acceptable and avoids implying calls are blocked)
